project.name: Chapeltown
project.boundarySource: Mapped named-place location with a conservative editorial study buffer
project.researchNotes: Full strict-boundary audit. Chapeltown remains selector-only at 28 and does not appear on the town map. It was reconciled directly against the local HES scheduled-monument polygons: none intersects the strict boundary; nearby SM5987, SM5989, SM5990 and SM5991 remain outside and are not imported. LB11289 is complete and now dated as a medieval chapel/burial ground rebuilt in the 19th century. Seven NRHE records with explicit prehistoric, Neolithic, medieval or post-medieval classifications now carry broad, qualified date ranges and are visible. The period-unassigned Kinblethmont kennels remain intact but hidden. No qualifying public See card, café/coffee-and-cake stop, named local trail, picnic facility, visitor parking or public toilet was verified. Nearby Inverkeilor venues and Kinblethmont estate attractions are outside the boundary. Angus-wide full audit completed 2026-09-01: all six visitor categories, the four named commercial trail providers, current official/conventional routes, strict-boundary scoring and local HES/NRHE integrity were checked.

touristAppeal.label: Minor Interest
touristAppeal.summary: A small crossroads hamlet with a medieval chapel/burial-place landscape and cropmark archaeology, but no managed attraction or visitor-service cluster.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: No dedicated dog visit or managed public access was verified; respect private burial and agricultural land.

townGuide.characterTag: Crossroads hamlet and buried medieval landscape
townGuide.headline: Historic context without a developed visitor stop
townGuide.intro: Chapeltown remains a 28% selector-only locality. Its medieval chapel and burial-ground history is genuine, but the enclosure is a private burial place and the surrounding archaeology is largely buried cropmark evidence.

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Respect private land
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Do not treat the burial place or surrounding cropmark fields as a managed attraction, parking site or public trail.

townGuide.visitorMood: A historically layered but largely private agricultural hamlet.
